candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Convert mixed numbers and/or whole numbers into equivalent improper fractions (or whole numbers as fractions with a specified denominator) to enable subtraction.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three codebooks describe rewriting mixed numbers a b/c as (ac+b)/c and rewriting whole numbers as fractions with a chosen denominator prior to computation.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Determine a common denominator (often via LCM) and rewrite each fraction as an equivalent fraction with that shared denominator.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: Each expert includes both selecting/using an LCM (or other common denominator) and scaling numerators/denominators to create equivalent fractions with the same denominator.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Compute the difference once quantities are in compatible form (same denominator and/or separated whole and fractional parts), producing the unsimplified result.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three focus on the actual subtraction step after compatibility is achieved (subtract numerators over a shared denominator and/or subtract whole and fractional parts separately).

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Reduce the computed result to simplest accepted form by simplifying to lowest terms and/or converting between improper fractions, mixed numbers, and integers.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three include post-subtraction simplification (reduce by common factors, recognize already simplest/equals 0 or 1) and formatting the final answer (mixed number/integer as appropriate).

alignment_summary: All skill_ids across A, B, and C align cleanly into four shared concepts with full (3/3) consensus: (1) converting mixed/whole numbers to fractional forms for computation, (2) finding/using a common denominator via equivalent fractions, (3) performing the subtraction once compatible, and (4) simplifying/formatting the final result.
